html:
The Tzotzil are a Maya people of the central highlands of Chiapas in southern Mexico. Their language belongs to the Mayan languages and is closely related to that of the Tzeltal, their eastern neighbours.

Before the conquest they lived in towns such as Zinacantán, a trading power that dealt in salt and amber with the Aztec merchants. Spaniards conquered the highlands in the 1520s and founded the town now called San Cristóbal de las Casas. Tzotzil communities kept their language and a blend of Maya and Catholic religion; Chamula and Zinacantán remain known for their own customs and dress.

In 1712 Tzotzil and Tzeltal towns rose in a great revolt against Spanish rule. In 1994 many joined the Zapatista uprising, and in 1997 paramilitaries killed 45 Tzotzil villagers at Acteal. Today they number several hundred thousand in Mexico.
